name: Aortic Dissection Syndromes
aliases: Connective Tissue Disorders Predisposing to Aortic Dissection

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Revised Ghent Criteria (for Marfan Syndrome) and Clinical Criteria for Heritable Aortopathies

criteria.description: Aortic root dilation or aneurysm detected by imaging
Family history of aortic dissection or related connective tissue disorders
Ectopia lentis (dislocation of the ocular lens)
Presence of systemic connective tissue features such as skeletal abnormalities (e.g., arachnodactyly, pectus deformities)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with aortic dissection syndromes (e.g., FBN1, TGFBR1/2, COL3A1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of aortic root dilation or dissection plus either a pathogenic genetic variant or characteristic systemic features or family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of clinical, imaging, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sudden severe chest or back pain
pathognomonic.notes: Described as tearing or ripping in nature

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
Neurological deficits from stroke or spinal ischemia
Abdominal pain from extension of dissection

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying pathogenic variants (e.g., FBN1, TGFBR1/2, COL3A1)
imaging: CT angiography showing intimal flap and false lumen
MRI/MRA demonstrating aortic root dilation and dissection
Echocardiography revealing aortic root aneurysm and valve involvement
other: Family history of sudden cardiac death or aortic dissection
Physical examination findings of connective tissue disorder features

distinguishingFeatures: Prominent skeletal features including tall stature and arachnodactyly
Thin, translucent skin with visible veins
Hypertelorism and bifid uvula or cleft palate
Aggressive vascular disease with widespread aneurysms

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe chest or back pain
Pulse deficits or blood pressure discrepancies between limbs
Signs of acute limb ischemia or neurological deficits
references: Erbel R, Aboyans V, Boileau C, et al. 2014 ESC Guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of aortic diseases. Eur Heart J. 2014;35(41):2873-2926.
Loeys BL, Dietz HC, Braverman AC, et al. The revised Ghent nosology for the Marfan syndrome. J Med Genet. 2010;47(7):476-485.
Milewicz DM, Ramirez F. Therapies for thoracic aortic aneurysms and acute aortic dissections. Arterioscler Thromb Vasc Biol. 2019;39(2):126-136.
